archetypes.name: ledger-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces a new ledger row kind and JSON aggregation contract that can silently drift from existing 13-column parsing rules.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the proposed record-round row layout, validation rules, and timing-report aggregation match the current timing ledger/report implementation and documented contracts. Look for schema mismatches, field-order ambiguity, attachment logic gaps, or places where existing markdown/summary paths might accidentally consume round rows. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: publish-surface
archetypes.rationale: The value depends on round data reaching committed run logs, especially for design where publish ordering is called out as fragile.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check whether the plan correctly targets the run-log flush and publish surfaces for implement and design without adding unnecessary flush sites. Pay special attention to design-publish ordering, timing-report-final.json freshness, SESSION_ID gating, stderr/warning handling, and whether committed batches actually pick up the richer timing JSON. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: round-semantics
archetypes.rationale: Round durations and counts come from different loop branches and artifacts, making off-by-one, stale-file, and undercount errors likely.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the plan covers every implement and design review-round exit path where timing should be emitted, including failed panels, legacy single-pass mode, revise/post-apply paths, continuations, and terminal exits. Compare the proposed count sources against the actual artifacts and environment variables so accepted, rejected, and design OOS values cannot be stale or counted from the wrong file. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
